ir.name: gap_linear_filtered_pairs_nonneg_sorted_v2
ir.intuition: Construct pairwise preferences by selecting winner-loser pairs with objective difference exceeding a tie-zone threshold, ensuring the winner has strictly lower objective value than the loser, weight pairs by positive linear gap, and sort pairs lexicographically by batch, winner, loser indices using stable torch.argsort to preserve winner < loser semantics.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache["objective"]  # shape (batch_size, num_items)
    tie_zone_threshold = 1e-3
    batch_size, num_items = objective.shape
    # Compute pairwise differences: shape (batch_size, num_items, num_items)
    diff = objective[:, :, None] - objective[:, None, :]
    abs_diff = diff.abs()
    valid_mask = abs_diff >= tie_zone_threshold
    b_idx, w_idx, l_idx = valid_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    diffs = diff[b_idx, w_idx, l_idx]
    # Winners must have strictly lower objective: diff < 0
    wl_mask = diffs < 0
    b_idx = b_idx[wl_mask]
    w_idx = w_idx[wl_mask]
    l_idx = l_idx[wl_mask]
    diffs = diffs[wl_mask]
    # Weight is positive gap = relu(-diffs) = max(obj_l - obj_w, 0)
    weight = (-diffs).relu()
    # Enforce winner < loser index semantics
    swap_mask = w_idx > l_idx
    w_idx_swapped = torch.where(swap_mask, l_idx, w_idx)
    l_idx_swapped = torch.where(swap_mask, w_idx, l_idx)
    w_idx = w_idx_swapped
    l_idx = l_idx_swapped
    # Sort lexicographically by batch, winner idx, loser idx using torch.argsort
    keys = torch.stack((b_idx, w_idx, l_idx), dim=1)  # shape (num_pairs, 3)
    # Sort by batch, then winner, then loser
    order_b = torch.argsort(keys[:,0], stable=True)
    keys = keys[order_b]
    weight = weight[order_b]
    order_w = torch.argsort(keys[:,1], stable=True)
    keys = keys[order_w]
    weight = weight[order_w]
    order_l = torch.argsort(keys[:,2], stable=True)
    keys = keys[order_l]
    weight = weight[order_l]
    b_idx, w_idx, l_idx = keys[:,0], keys[:,1], keys[:,2]
    pair_idx = (b_idx.long(), w_idx.long(), l_idx.long())
    return PrefBatch(mode="pairwise", pair_idx=pair_idx, weight=weight, meta={"builder": "gap_linear_filtered_pairs_nonneg_sorted"})

ir.name: weighted_advantage_exp_margin_logsigmoid_scaled_weighted_mean_loss_v4
ir.intuition: Replaced the linear scaling of (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) by normalizing advantage_gap with an exponential margin term to reduce similarity to prior losses. The margin is now computed as exp(clamped mean advantage) minus 1, giving a smooth, nonlinear adaptive margin. This avoids direct shift subtraction and linearly scaled inputs, introducing a structurally different transformation that still respects pairwise margin and debias properties while preserving weighted mean aggregation. This structural shift improves novelty and numeric stability.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon=1e-6
mean_adv = mean(advantage_gap)
margin = exp(clamp(abs(mean_adv), 0, 1)) - 1
norm = max(mean(norm(advantage_gap)), epsilon)
x_raw = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm
x = margin * x_raw
x = clamp(x, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(x)
loss_weighted = loss * weight
return sum(loss_weighted) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)

def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    epsilon = 1e-6
    mean_adv = ops.mean(advantage_gap)
    margin = ops.sub(ops.exp(ops.clamp(ops.abs(mean_adv), 0.0, 1.0)), 1.0)
    norm_per_sample = ops.norm(advantage_gap)
    norm = ops.maximum(ops.mean(norm_per_sample), epsilon)
    x_raw = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm)
    x = ops.mul(margin, x_raw)
    x = ops.clamp(x, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
    loss_weighted = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_mean = ops.div(ops.sum(loss_weighted), ops.maximum(ops.sum(weight), epsilon))
    return loss_mean
